title: APEC 2026: Let’s get back to the future on trade
gist: With the WTO hamstrung and trade-agreement rules being ignored, the author (Australian APEC Study Centre) argues Australia should revive APEC's 1990s voluntary 'pathfinder' model — starting with bilateral Australia-China pilots — on practical business frictions like product traceability standards, skills mobility and SME-relevant digital services, around China's 2026 APEC hosting in Shenzhen.

insights.claim: The World Trade Organisation is hamstrung, many regional trade agreements based on its rules are being ignored, and trust in institutions is eroding, making it harder to manage geopolitical, technological and demographic change in trade.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Rules-based trade is no longer a reliable anchor; expect more ad hoc, plurilateral arrangements.
insights.quote: The World Trade Organisation, also a child of the 1990s, is hamstrung.

insights.claim: The WTO's 2026 Annual Report noted that open medium-sized economies like Australia have the most to lose when global rules don't work.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Middle-economy exporters (Australia) carry asymmetric downside from rules erosion — relevant for AUD and export-sector risk.

insights.claim: APEC's voluntary Pathfinder approach, first adopted in the 1990s, lets willing economies progress specific issues without requiring all 21 members, with others able to join later as benefits are demonstrated.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Coalition-of-the-willing trade pilots are the realistic path for Asia-Pacific trade liberalisation in the near term.
insights.locator: Officials, academia and businesses in Australia

insights.claim: Pathfinder initiatives are not a replacement for the existing trade architecture but can act as building blocks toward convergence and, longer term, toward APEC's free trade area of the Asia Pacific (FTAAP) vision.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: FTAAP remains a long-dated aspiration; incremental pilots are where real movement would show first.
insights.locator: While not a replacement for the existing

insights.claim: Because even launching multilateral pathfinders is difficult, the author suggests bilateral pilot initiatives — notably between Australia and China — as a starting point.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Signals appetite in Australian policy circles for practical economic re-engagement with China.
insights.quote: Bilateral pilot initiatives can be a good place to start.

insights.claim: China is hosting APEC in 2026 with leaders meeting in Shenzhen in November under the theme 'Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together', and consensus on official outcomes is not expected to be easy.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Low expectations for formal APEC outcomes; watch for side pilots or bilateral deliverables.
insights.locator: This year China is hosting APEC

insights.claim: Australian business leaders cite opaque and shifting compliance requirements, diverging professional and technical standards, fragmented product traceability requirements and unpredictable rule application as daily market-access barriers.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Non-tariff barriers, not tariffs, are the binding constraint for many exporters.

insights.claim: Overlapping trade agreements have become so complex that using them is sometimes not worth the effort, and smaller firms are disproportionately affected.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Low FTA utilisation rates mean headline trade deals overstate real market access, especially for SMEs.
insights.quote: Overlapping trade agreements and how they fit together have also become a source of complexity, sometimes not worth the effort.

insights.claim: Proposed pilot areas include aligning technical standards for product traceability and authentication in green technology, sector-specific temporary skills mobility for infrastructure projects, mapping trade-agreement commitments on digital services for SMEs, and AI use in health diagnostics.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Green-tech traceability standards and AI-in-health are candidate early-harmonisation sectors to watch.
insights.locator: Some of these issues could be tackled

insights.claim: Work across APEC officials, business and academia is addressing AI's impact on trade, ageing populations, the growing role of services, the green transition and the digital economy.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Indicates the policy agenda shaping future Asia-Pacific trade rules.

insights.claim: The ideas came from a dialogue at RMIT University involving the Australian APEC Study Centre, the Australian Pacific Economic Cooperation Committee, the China APEC Study Centre at Nankai University and the China National Committee for Pacific Economic Cooperation.
insights.speaker: Kristen Bondietti
insights.so_what: Track-2 Australia-China economic dialogue is active, a leading indicator of official re-engagement.
